messages:
maya: hey team — quick one. im stuck at the airport, my flight's delayed. i'm primary tonight 00:00-08:00 UTC but there's a ~4hr window (00:00-04:00) I can't reliably cover. can someone pick up primary or shadow the first half? sorry for the short notice :grimacing:

liam: pinging to check — do we have any scheduled maintenance or capacity changes that would make that window risky?

maya: good q — no planned deploys in that window afaik. infra ran a rolling kernel update earlier today but all green. still, last-week we saw a small 5xx blip in /v1/generate for eu-west during midnight. worth keeping an eye.

cheng: i can take primary for 00:00-02:30 UTC if that helps. after that i need to hand off to someone in APAC for the late chunk.

nina: i can cover 02:30-05:30 UTC (overlaps with cheng), then alex can take 05:30-08:00?

alex: im in on that final window, yes. ill be reachable on phone.

incident-bot: [AUTO] oncall_schedule check: maya is current primary until 08:00 UTC. Secondary: liam. Deputies: cheng, nina.

maya: thx cheng/nina/alex. to be explicit: handoff plan: cheng primary 00:00-02:30, nina 02:30-05:30, alex final. liam stays secondary for the whole night. is everybody OK with that?

liam: that plan works. quick note: secondary should monitor the EU 5xx rate (dashboard: https://app.datadog.com/dash/1234/eu-5xx) and be ready to escalate to dedicated pool fallback if latency > 250ms p50 and >1% 5xx.

nina: ack. do we want to enable auto-fallback to v2-small for the region if capacity drops?

cheng: i'd prefer manual before switching model variants — past toggles caused more client errors when configs mismatched. but if we see consistent queue depth > 200, do the fallback.

maya: runbook pointers for people picking up: https://confluence.redwood/oncall/handoff-runbook
maya: key bits: 1) check redis-kv cache hit rate, 2) check batcher queue length on serving nodes, 3) watch for elevated token generation tail latencies.

alex: can you paste the single-line cmd to rotate pages/assign primary? make it quick for when we actually swap.

ops-bot: To assign primary via CLI run: `redwood oncall assign --user <username> --role primary --until <UTC-timestamp>`

cheng: thanks. for handoffs we usually do `redwood oncall assign --user cheng --role primary --until 2026-03-15T02:30:00Z` then add a slack confirmation reaction.

liam: also remember to update the incident channel summary snippet so SRE duty knows who to escalate to. we had a missed escalation last month because the handoff msg was buried.

maya: good point. after you assign, post the single-line summary in #incidents: "primary: cheng 00:00-02:30 UTC | secondary: liam" and pin it.

nina: will do. one more: if you get pages that look like rate-limit throttles vs actual 5xx, check edge-proxy logs first — sometimes it's an upstream quota. use `gzcat /var/log/proxy/* | grep request_id` sample.

alex: want to confirm pager routes — are customer-facing pages (prod-critical) still routing to primary+secondary by default?

incident-bot: [ROUTE] prod-critical -> primary, secondary, oncall-manager. Suppression windows: none currently.

maya: FYI — i've already muted low-priority alerts for the 00:00-04:00 window for my user, but that doesn't stop real pages. so pls don't mute.

cheng: quick status: im going to assign myself now and post the summary.

ops-bot: `redwood oncall assign --user cheng --role primary --until 2026-03-15T02:30:00Z` executed by cheng at 2026-03-15T00:01:12Z

cheng: assigned and posted in #incidents.

nina: assigning myself for 02:30-05:30 now.

ops-bot: `redwood oncall assign --user nina --role primary --until 2026-03-15T05:30:00Z` executed by nina at 2026-03-15T02:28:40Z

nina: pinned the incident summary. added the quick checklist in the pinned note (redis, batcher, model-queue, fallback plan).

liam: thanks all. small reminder — if you see a latency spike but 5xx is low, check KV cache hit ratio: < 80% suggests prefix cache miss, see runbook section 3.2 for cache warmup commands.

maya: one more — if anything escalates and we need a bridge, use `#incident-bridge` and call out "bridge requested: primary X, secondary Y, impact: X% 5xx, regions" so oncall-manager can join quickly.

alex: i'm online for my window. i've added my mobile to the pager. if things look dicey after 05:30, i'd like to handoff to cheng again or call for rotation.

incident-bot: [AUTO] alert suppressed: maintenance-window (none) — no action.

maya: thanks everyone. i'll update here if flight changes again but otherwise i'm relieved. appreciate the quick shuffle and sorry for the scramble. :pray:

liam: all good. logging this thread into the oncall notes for future retros.

ops-bot: [REMINDER] Handoff checklist auto-reminder will post 15m before each assignment end.

nina: noted. i'll run through the checklist before handing to alex.

cheng: good luck — ping me if you need a warm-handoff voice call.

alex: thanks — fun little test of the rotation.

maya: closing the loop: flight took off, ETA 07:10 UTC. thanks again team.
